chunks: Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd ibn Ḥukaym narrated to me from Salamah ibn Khaťťāb, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from ‘Ammār ibn Mūsā Al-Sābāťi, from Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about praying in the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), is it like praying in Madīnah? He (peace be upon him) replied, 'No, because one prayer in the Mosque of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family) is equal to one thousand prayers, and praying in Madīnah is like praying in other cities.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in reward between praying in the Prophet's Mosque and other mosques in Madinah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes the unique spiritual status of the Prophet’s Mosque (Masjid al-Nabawi) by assigning it a reward of one thousand prayers, setting it apart from the general merit of Madīnah, which is equivalent to other cities. This hadith underscores the hierarchical sanctity of the Prophet’s burial place within Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that while Madīnah is blessed, the specific locus of the Prophet’s presence holds a singular, elevated virtue. Such distinctions guide believers in prioritizing visits (Ziyarat) to the Prophet’s shrine for maximum spiritual recompense.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 6. Ḥukaym ibn Dāwūd ibn Ḥukaym narrated to me from Salamah ibn Khaťťāb, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from ‘Ammār ibn Mūsā Al-Sābāťi, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)), “Is praying in the Mosque of the Prophet (s.a.a.w.) the same as praying anywhere else in Madīnah?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “No. One Salāt (prayer) in the Mosque of the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) is equal to one thousand prayers elsewhere. However, praying anywhere else in Madīnah is just like praying in any other city.”
